source.title: FLM-101B: An Open LLM and How to Train It with $100K Budget
source.authors: Xiang Li; Yiqun Yao; Xin Jiang; Xue-Zhi Fang; Xu-Ying Meng; Si-Qi Fan; Peng Han; Jing Li; LI DU; Bo-Wen Qin; Zheng Zhang; Aixin Sun; Yequan Wang

record.file_problem: None noted; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports a proxy-width loss-prediction result relevant to extrapolation and evaluates downstream benchmark performance across three growth stages, but it does not reproduce a fixed-size scaling-law sweep.
record.gate_note: The paper cites scaling-law and µP work and uses those ideas in its training-stability approach. Its own results include a qualitative proxy-to-FLM-16B loss-prediction statement, a training-loss curve during progressive growth, and downstream scores across growth stages. The cited scaling-law findings and benchmark comparisons in other tables are not treated as new scaling-law results. Figure 2 concerns training loss, not held-out loss, and gives no numerical loss values.
record.test_reason: This is a model-training report for FLM-101B. It uses µP plus a modified scaling law (via µScaling) as a tool for hyperparameter transfer and stability. Its only scaling-related statement is one unquantified sentence that FLM-16B's loss range was predictable from proxy widths. The Table 6 stage scores evaluate the authors' own growth method. They come from three sequential checkpoints of one run, where size and cumulative tokens (about 245B, 285B and 312B) rise together. No power-law fit, prediction error, or independent size sweep is reported, so no version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right, but the main conclusion is about cost. A growth strategy trained FLM-101B for about $100K, reaching about 80% of baseline performance with about 10% of their FLOPs. It is competitive on knowledge and IQ-inspired benchmarks, and training was stable via µP-transferred hyperparameters and function-preserving growth. The stage-wise gains are framed as evidence of knowledge inheritance across growth, not as a scaling law. The proxy loss prediction is a side remark.
record.recipe_differences: This study trains a progressively grown model and evaluates its stages; it does not independently train fixed-size models across parameter, token, or compute sweeps to fit the original scaling-law relations.
record.method_sensitivity: The authors say growth schedules, growth operators, and data amounts were not explored adequately. The evaluated stages also differ in size and stage token allocation.

fits_no_version.finding: The training-loss curve becomes steeper after each function-preserving growth step (16B→51B→101B).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In progressive-growth training, loss reduction per step increases after parameter growth.

fits_no_version.finding: Open LLM average rises 39.19→41.79→44.41 across the 16B/51B/101B growth stages. Size and cumulative tokens increase together.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Benchmark scores of a progressively grown model improve across growth stages, indicating knowledge inheritance; this is not a fixed-size scaling result.

record.problems: The proxy-loss prediction is described without numerical predictions or errors. The growth-stage evaluation is not an independent size sweep: checkpoints inherit from earlier stages, and model size, stage, and token allocation vary together. The training-loss curve has no reported numerical values.

untested.parts: All of it: no held-out loss versus parameters, tokens or compute.
All of it: the proxy-to-16B loss prediction is asserted but not quantified.
All of it: no compute-optimal allocation analysis.
All of it: no shape comparison.
All of it: three confounded checkpoints of one run, with no predictor of downstream score from scale or loss.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests/T2' and its V2/V6 labels are not supported. The V2 label rested on a row with no numbers, and the V6 label on three sequential checkpoints of a single run, which is an evaluation of the authors' own method. Re-tranched as T4 with no verdicts.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out loss power laws across parameters, tokens, or compute and over several orders of magnitude.
No numerical prediction errors, fitted exponents, or detailed comparison between predicted and observed losses are reported.
No compute-budget sweep or loss-minimising parameter/token allocation is measured.
No controlled comparison of architecture shape at fixed parameter count.
No tests of other modalities, repeated data, fine-tuning, or transfer as scaling-law regimes.
The paper reports stage-wise benchmark scores, not a quantitative predictor relating downstream performance to scale or held-out pretraining loss.
No analysis of how fitting choices alter exponents or compute-optimal allocation, or of departures from a single power law.

rows.subject: FLM-16B
rows.operation_detail: Use proxy-width results to predict the loss range of FLM-16B at matching training steps.

conditions.value: multiple proxy widths at the same steps

rows.value: The authors state that the FLM-16B loss range is predictable from multiple proxy widths at the same steps; numerical prediction results are not provided.
rows.note: The text describes µP transfer and a modified scaling-law approach, but does not give fitted power laws or prediction errors.
rows.check: The row is on topic for V2, but the study gives no predicted or observed loss values and no errors. The text says only that the loss range 'is also predictable', so 'partial' cannot be read from it. This is the use of a cited method (µScaling) as a tool, not a test.

rows.subject: FLM-101B
rows.operation_detail: Report training loss over processed tokens during progressive growth.
rows.value: The text says the loss curve becomes steeper after each growth; numerical values are figure only.
rows.note: This is training loss during progressive growth, not a measurement of held-out loss following a power law.
rows.check: This is training loss during progressive growth, shown in a figure only. It is not held-out loss against N, D or C. Linking it to no version is correct.

rows.subject: FLM-16B
rows.operation_detail: Evaluate the 16B growth-stage checkpoint on Open LLM tasks.
rows.note: This is one checkpoint in the authors' progressive growth sequence, not an independently trained size.
rows.check: These are sequential checkpoints of one grown model, not independently trained sizes. Parameter count and cumulative tokens are confounded. The 'training tokens' condition gives per-stage tokens (245.37B, 39.64B, 26.54B), but the cumulative totals are about 245B, 285B and 312B. Baselines should be the previous stage, not 'not stated'. The rows evaluate the growth method and test no predictable downstream-scaling relation.
